CONSTRAINTS.constr_tol.name: constr_tol
CONSTRAINTS.constr_tol.description: Tolerance for keeping the constraints satisfied.

CONSTRAINTS.constr_type.name: constr_type
CONSTRAINTS.constr_type.description:
Type of constrain :

'type_coord'      : constraint on global coordination-number, i.e. the
                    average number of atoms of type B surrounding the
                    atoms of type A. The coordination is defined by
                    using a Fermi-Dirac.
                    (four indexes must be specified).

'atom_coord'      : constraint on local coordination-number, i.e. the
                    average number of atoms of type A surrounding a
                    specific atom. The coordination is defined by
                    using a Fermi-Dirac.
                    (four indexes must be specified).

'distance'        : constraint on interatomic distance
                    (two atom indexes must be specified).

'planar_angle'    : constraint on planar angle
                    (three atom indexes must be specified).

'torsional_angle' : constraint on torsional angle
                    (four atom indexes must be specified).

'bennett_proj'    : constraint on the projection onto a given direction
                    of the vector defined by the position of one atom
                    minus the center of mass of the others.
                    ( Ch.H. Bennett in Diffusion in Solids, Recent
                      Developments, Ed. by A.S. Nowick and J.J. Burton,
                      New York 1975 ).

CONSTRAINTS.constr_target.name: constr_target
CONSTRAINTS.constr_target.description:
Target for the constrain ( angles are specified in degrees ).
This variable is optional.

OCCUPATIONS.f_inp1.name: f_inp1
OCCUPATIONS.f_inp1.description:
Occupations of individual states (MAX 10 PER LINE).
For spin-polarized calculations, these are majority spin states.

OCCUPATIONS.f_inp2.name: f_inp2
OCCUPATIONS.f_inp2.description:
Occupations of minority spin states (MAX 10 PER LINE)
To be specified only for spin-polarized calculations.

ATOMIC_FORCES.fx.name: fx

&INPUT.max_out_wfc.description:
Maximum number of atomic wavefunctions written in the output
file.

&INPUT.noscf.name: noscf

if .true. the charge is not computed. The occupations are
not used and the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions are those
of a hydrogen-like atom.

&INPUT.lsd.name: lsd

0 ... non spin polarized calculation

BEWARE:

not allowed if

=3 (PP generation) or with full
relativistic calculation

Exchange-correlation functional.

Examples:

'BLYP'
  ...

For the complete list, see module "functionals" in ../Modules/
The default is 
'PZ'
 for all-electron calculations,
it is read from the PP file in a PP calculation.

&INPUT.latt.name: latt
&INPUT.latt.description:
0 ... no Latter correction
1 ... apply Latter correction

&INPUT.isic.name: isic
&INPUT.isic.description:
0 ... no Self-interaction correction
1 ... apply Self-interaction correction

&INPUT.rytoev_fact.name: rytoev_fact
&INPUT.rytoev_fact.description: Factor used to convert Ry into eV.

&INPUT.cau_fact.name: cau_fact
&INPUT.cau_fact.description:
Speed of light in a.u..

(Be careful the default value is always used in the
 relativistic exchange.)

&INPUT.vdw.name: vdw
&INPUT.vdw.description:
If .true., the frequency dependent polarizability and van der
Waals coefficient C6 will be computed in Thomas-Fermi and
von Weizsaecker approximation(only for closed-shell ions).

&INPUT.prefix.name: prefix
&INPUT.prefix.description:
Prefix for file names - only for output file names
containing the orbitals, logarithmic derivatives, tests
See below for file names and the content of the file.

&INPUT.verbosity.name: verbosity
&INPUT.verbosity.description:
'low'
 or 
'high'


if 
'high'
 with 
iswitch
=2,3 prints separately core and
valence contributions to the energies. Print the
frozen-core energy.

&INPUT.file_charge.name: file_charge
&INPUT.file_charge.description:
Name of the file where the code writes the all-electron
total charge. No charge is written if file_charge=' '.

&INPUT.config.name: config
&INPUT.config.description:
A string with the electronic configuration.

Example:
  '[Ar] 3d10 4s2 4p2.5'

* If 
lsd
=1, spin-up and spin-down state may appear twice
  with the respective occupancy: 3p4 3p2 = 4 up,
  2 down. Otherwise, the Hund's rule is assumed.

* If 
rel
=2, states with jj=l-1/2 are filled first.
  If a state appears twice, the first one has jj=l-1/2,
  the second one jj=l+1/2 (except S states)
  (Use rel_dist if you want to average the electrons
  over all available states.)

* If config='default' the code uses 
zed
 to set the ground
  state electronic configuration for the atom.

Negative occupancies are used to flag unbound states;
they are not actually used.

&INPUT.relpert.name: relpert
&INPUT.relpert.description:
If .true. the relativistic corrections to the non-relativistic
Kohn-Sham energy levels (
rel
=0 .and. 
lsd
=0) are computed using
first-order perturbation theory in all-electron calculations.
The corrections consist of the following terms:
   E_vel: velocity (p^4) correction
   E_Dar: Darwin term
   E_S-O: spin-orbit coupling
The spin-orbit term vanishes for s-electron states and gives
rise to a splitting of (2*l+1)*E_S-O for the other states.
The separate contributions are printed only if verbosity='high'.

Formulas and notation are based on the Herman-Skillman book:
F. Herman and S. Skillman, "Atomic Structure Calculations",
Prentice-Hall, Inc., Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, 1963

&INPUT.rel_dist.name: rel_dist
&INPUT.rel_dist.description:
'energy'
 or 
'average'


* if 
'energy'
 the relativistic l-1/2 states are filled first.

* if 
'average'
 the electrons are uniformly distributed
  among all the states with the given l.

&INPUT.write_coulomb.name: write_coulomb
&INPUT.write_coulomb.description:
If .true., a fake pseudo-potential file with name X.UPF,
where X is the atomic symbol, is written. It contains
the radial grid and the wavefunctions as specified in input,
plus the info needed to build the Coulomb potential
for an all-electron calculation - for testing only.

&INPUTP.zval.name: zval
&INPUTP.zval.description:
Valence charge.

zval is automatically calculated from available data.
If the value of zval is provided in input, it will be
checked versus the calculated value. The only case in
which you need to explicitly provide the value of zval
for noninteger zval (i.e. half core-hole pseudo-potentials).

&INPUTP.pseudotype.name: pseudotype
&INPUTP.pseudotype.description:
1 ... norm-conserving, single-projector PP
      
IMPORTANT:
 if pseudotype=1 all calculations are done
      using the SEMILOCAL form, not the separable nonlocal form

2 ... norm-conserving PP in separable form (obsolescent)
      All calculations are done using SEPARABLE non-local form
      
IMPORTANT:
 multiple projectors allowed but not properly
      implemented, use only if you know what you are doing

3 ... ultrasoft PP or PAW

&INPUTP.file_pseudopw.name: file_pseudopw
&INPUTP.file_pseudopw.description:
File where the generated PP is written.

* if the file name ends with "upf" or "UPF",
or in any case for spin-orbit PP (rel=2),
the file is written in UPF format;

* if the file name ends with 'psp' it is
written in native CPMD format (this is currently
an experimental feature); otherwise it is written
in the old "NC" format if pseudotype=1, or
in the old RRKJ format if pseudotype=2 or 3
(no default, must be specified).

&INPUTP.file_recon.name: file_recon
&INPUTP.file_recon.description:
File containing data needed for GIPAW reconstruction
of all-electron wavefunctions from PP results.
If you want to use additional states to perform the
reconstruction, add them at the end of the list
of all-electron states.

&INPUTP.lloc.name: lloc
&INPUTP.lloc.description:
Angular momentum of the local channel.

* lloc=-1 or lloc=-2 pseudizes the all-electron potential
  if lloc=-2 the original recipe of Troullier-Martins
  is used (zero first and second derivatives at r=0)
* lloc>-1 uses the corresponding channel as local PP

NB: if lloc>-1, the corresponding channel must be the last in the
list of wavefunctions appearing after the namelist &inputp
In the relativistic case, if lloc > 0 both the j=lloc-1/2 and
the j=lloc+1/2 wavefunctions must be at the end of the list.

&INPUTP.rcloc.name: rcloc
&INPUTP.rcloc.default:
Must be specified only iflloc=-1, otherwise the
corresponding value ofrcutis used.
&INPUTP.rcloc.description: Matching radius (a.u.) for local pseudo-potential (no default).

&INPUTP.nlcc.name: nlcc
&INPUTP.nlcc.description:
If .true. produce a PP with the nonlinear core
correction of Louie, Froyen, and Cohen
[
PRB 26, 1738 (1982)
].

&INPUTP.new_core_ps.name: new_core_ps
&INPUTP.new_core_ps.description: If .true. pseudizes the core charge with bessel functions.

&INPUTP.rcore.name: rcore
&INPUTP.rcore.description:
Matching radius (a.u.) for the smoothing of the core charge.
If not specified, the matching radius is determined
by the condition:  rho_core(rcore) = 2*rho_valence(rcore)

&INPUTP.tm.name: tm
&INPUTP.tm.description:
* .true. for Troullier-Martins pseudization [
PRB 43, 1993 (1991)
]

* .false. for Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos pseudization
  [
PRB 41, 1227 (1990)
, erratum 
PRB 44, 13175 (1991)
]

&INPUTP.rho0.name: rho0
&INPUTP.rho0.description:
Charge at the origin: when the Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos
method with 3 Bessel functions fails, specifying rho0 > 0
may allow to override the problem (using 4 Bessel functions).
Typical values are in the order of 0.01-0.02

&INPUTP.lpaw.name: lpaw
&INPUTP.lpaw.description:
If .true. produce a PAW dataset, experimental feature
only for 
pseudotype
=3

&INPUTP.which_augfun.name: which_augfun
&INPUTP.which_augfun.default: 'AE'for Vanderbilt-Ultrasoft pseudo-potentials and 'BESSEL' for PAW datasets.
&INPUTP.which_augfun.description:
If different from 
'AE'
 the augmentation functions are pseudized
before 
rmatch_augfun
. The pseudization options are:

* 
'PSQ'
        Use Bessel functions to pseudize Q
               from the origin to rmatch_augfun.

These features are available only for PAW:

* 
'BESSEL'
     Use Bessel functions to pseudize the Q.
* 
'GAUSS'
      Use 2 Gaussian functions to pseudize the Q.
* 
'BG'
         Use original Bloechl's recipe with a single gaussian.

Note: if lpaw is true and which_augfun is set to AE real all-
electron charge will be used, which will produce extremely
hard augmentation.

&INPUTP.rmatch_augfun.name: rmatch_augfun
&INPUTP.rmatch_augfun.description:
Pseudization radius for the augmentation functions. Presently
it has the same value for all L.

&INPUTP.rmatch_augfun_nc.name: rmatch_augfun_nc
&INPUTP.rmatch_augfun_nc.description:
If .true. the augmentation functions are pseudized
from the origin to min(rcut(ns),rcut(ns1)) where ns
and ns1 are the two channels for that Q. In this case
rmatch_augfun is not used.

&INPUTP.lsave_wfc.name: lsave_wfc
&INPUTP.lsave_wfc.description:
Set it to .true. to save all-electron and pseudo wavefunctions
used in the pseudo-potential generation in the UPF file. Only
works for UPFv2 format.

&INPUTP.lgipaw_reconstruction.name: lgipaw_reconstruction
&INPUTP.lgipaw_reconstruction.description:
Set it to .true. to generate pseudo-potentials containing the
additional info required for reconstruction of all-electron
orbitals, used by GIPAW. You will typically need to specify
additional projectors beyond those used in the generation of
pseudo-potentials. You should also specify 
file_recon
.

All projectors used in the reconstruction must be listed BOTH
in the test configuration after namelist &test AND in the
all-electron configuration (variable 'config', namelist &inputp,
Use negative occupancies for projectors on unbound states). The
core radii in the test configuration should be the same as in
the pseudo-potential generation section and will be used as the
radius of reconstruction. Projectors not used to generate the
pseudo-potential should have zero occupation number.

&INPUTP.use_paw_as_gipaw.name: use_paw_as_gipaw
&INPUTP.use_paw_as_gipaw.description:
When generating a PAW dataset, setting this option to .true. will
save the core all-electron wavefunctions to the UPF file.
The GIPAW reconstruction to be performed using the PAW data and
projectors for the valence wavefunctions.

In the default case, the GIPAW valence wavefunction and projectors
are independent from the PAW ones and must be then specified as
explained above in lgipaw_reconstruction.

Setting this to .true. always implies 
lgipaw_reconstruction
 = .true.

&INPUTP.file_chi.name: file_chi
&INPUTP.file_chi.description: file containing output PP chi functions

&INPUTP.file_beta.name: file_beta
&INPUTP.file_beta.description: file containing output PP beta functions

&INPUTP.file_qvan.name: file_qvan
&INPUTP.file_qvan.description: file containing output PP qvan functions

&INPUTP.file_core.name: file_core
&INPUTP.file_core.description: file containing output total and core charge

&INPUTP.file_wfcaegen.name: file_wfcaegen
&INPUTP.file_wfcaegen.description: file with the all-electron wfc for generation

&INPUTP.file_wfcncgen.name: file_wfcncgen
&INPUTP.file_wfcncgen.description: file with the norm-conserving wfc for generation

&INPUTP.file_wfcusgen.name: file_wfcusgen
&INPUTP.file_wfcusgen.description: file with the ultra-soft wfc for generation

&TEST.nconf.name: nconf
&TEST.nconf.description:
the number of configurations to be tested. For 
iswitch
=4 nconf=2

&TEST.file_pseudo.name: file_pseudo
&TEST.file_pseudo.description:
File containing the PP.

* If the file name contains  ".upf" or ".UPF",
the file is assumed to be in UPF format;

* else if the file name contains ".rrkj3" or ".RRKJ3",
the old RRKJ format is first tried;

* otherwise, the old NC format is read.


IMPORTANT:
 in the latter case, all calculations are done
using the SEMILOCAL form, not the separable nonlocal form.
Use the UPF format if you want to test the separable form!

&TEST.ecutmin.name: ecutmin
&TEST.ecutmin.description:
Parameters (Ry) used for test with a basis set of spherical
Bessel functions j_l(qr) . The hamiltonian at fixed scf
potential is diagonalized for various values of ecut:

ecutmin
, 
ecutmin
+
decut
, 
ecutmin
+2*
decut
 ... up to 
ecutmax
.
This yields an indication of convergence with the
corresponding plane-wave cutoff in solids, and shows
in an unambiguous way if there are "ghost" states

&TEST.ecutmax.name: ecutmax
&TEST.ecutmax.description:
Parameters (Ry) used for test with a basis set of spherical
Bessel functions j_l(qr) . The hamiltonian at fixed scf
potential is diagonalized for various values of ecut:

ecutmin
, 
ecutmin
+
decut
, 
ecutmin
+2*
decut
 ... up to 
ecutmax
.
This yields an indication of convergence with the
corresponding plane-wave cutoff in solids, and shows
in an unambiguous way if there are "ghost" states

&TEST.decut.name: decut
&TEST.decut.description:
Parameters (Ry) used for test with a basis set of spherical
Bessel functions j_l(qr) . The hamiltonian at fixed scf
potential is diagonalized for various values of ecut:

ecutmin
, 
ecutmin
+
decut
,

decut
 ... up to

.
This yields an indication of convergence with the

&TEST.rm.name: rm
&TEST.rm.description: Radius of the box used with spherical Bessel functions.

&TEST.frozen_core.name: frozen_core
&TEST.frozen_core.description:
If .true. only the core wavefunctions of the first
configuration are calculated. The eigenvalues, orbitals
and energies of the other configurations are calculated
with the core of the first configuration.
The first configuration must be spin-unpolarized.

&TEST.rcutv.name: rcutv
&TEST.rcutv.description:
Cutoff distance (CUT) for the inclusion of LDA-1/2 potential.
Needed (mandatory) only if 
iswitch
 = 4

ALLELECTRONCARDS.isw.description: the spin index (1-2) used only in the lsda case

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.nwfs.description: number of wavefunctions to be pseudized

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.nls.description: Wavefunction label (same as in the all-electron configuration).

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.nns.name: nns
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.nns.description:
Principal quantum number (referred to the PSEUDOPOTENTIAL case;
nns=1 for lowest s, nns=2 for lowest p, and so on).

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.ocs.name: ocs
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.ocs.description: Occupation number  (same as in the all-electron configuration).

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.ener.name: ener
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.ener.description:
Energy (Ry) used to pseudize the corresponding state.
If 0.d0, use the one-electron energy of the all-electron state.
Do not use 0.d0 for unbound states!

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.rcut.name: rcut
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.rcut.description: Matching radius (a.u.) for norm conserving PP.

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.rcutus.name: rcutus
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.rcutus.description: Matching radius (a.u.) for ultrasoft PP - only for pseudotype=3.

PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.jjs.name: jjs
PSEUDOPOTENTIALGENERATIONCARDS.jjs.description: The total angular momentum (0.0 is allowed for complete shells).

PSEUDOPOTENTIALTESTCARDS.iswts.name: iswts
PSEUDOPOTENTIALTESTCARDS.iswts.description: spin index (1 or 2, used in lsda case)

PSEUDOPOTENTIALTESTCARDS.jjts.name: jjts
PSEUDOPOTENTIALTESTCARDS.jjts.description: total angular momentum of the state

&INPUTHP.prefix.name: prefix
&INPUTHP.prefix.description:
Prepended to input/output filenames; must be the same
used in the calculation of unperturbed system.

&INPUTHP.outdir.name: outdir
&INPUTHP.outdir.default: value of theESPRESSO_TMPDIRenvironment variable if set;current directory ('./') otherwise

&INPUTHP.iverbosity.name: iverbosity
&INPUTHP.iverbosity.description:
= 1 : minimal output
= 2 : as above + symmetry matrices, final response
      matrices chi0 and chi1 and their inverse matrices,
      full U matrix
= 3 : as above + various detailed info about the NSCF
      calculation at k and k+q
= 4 : as above + response occupation matrices at every
      iteration and for every q point in the star

&INPUTHP.max_seconds.name: max_seconds
&INPUTHP.max_seconds.description: Maximum allowed run time before the job stops smoothly.

&INPUTHP.nq1.name: nq1
&INPUTHP.nq1.description:
Parameters of the Monkhorst-Pack grid (no offset).
Same meaning as for nk1, nk2, nk3 in the input of pw.x.

&INPUTHP.nq2.name: nq2
&INPUTHP.nq2.description:
Parameters of the Monkhorst-Pack grid (no offset).
Same meaning as for nk1, nk2, nk3 in the input of pw.x.

&INPUTHP.nq3.name: nq3
&INPUTHP.nq3.description:
Parameters of the Monkhorst-Pack grid (no offset).
Same meaning as for nk1, nk2, nk3 in the input of pw.x.

&INPUTHP.skip_equivalence_q.name: skip_equivalence_q
&INPUTHP.skip_equivalence_q.description:
If .true. then the HP code will skip the equivalence
analysis of q points, and thus the full grid of q points
will be used. Otherwise the symmetry is used to determine
equivalent q points (star of q), and then perform
calculations only for inequivalent q points.

&INPUTHP.determine_num_pert_only.name: determine_num_pert_only
&INPUTHP.determine_num_pert_only.description:
If .true. determines the number of perturbations
(i.e. which atoms will be perturbed) and exits smoothly
without performing any calculation. For DFT+U+V, it also
determines the indices of inter-site couples.

&INPUTHP.determine_q_mesh_only.name: determine_q_mesh_only
&INPUTHP.determine_q_mesh_only.description:
If .true. determines the number of q points
for a given perturbed atom and exits smoothly.
This keyword can be used only if perturb_only_atom
is set to .true.

&INPUTHP.find_atpert.name: find_atpert
&INPUTHP.find_atpert.description:
Method for searching of atoms which must be perturbed.
1 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms there are
    by analyzing unperturbed occupations.
2 = Find how many Hubbard atoms to perturb based on
    how many different Hubbard atomic types there are.
    Warning: atoms which have the same type but which
    are inequivalent by symmetry or which have different
    occupations will not be distinguished in this case
    (use option 1 or 3 instead).
3 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms
    there are using symmetry. Atoms which have the
    same type but are not equivalent by symmetry will
    be distinguished in this case.
4 = Perturb all Hubbard atoms (the most expensive option)

&INPUTHP.docc_thr.name: docc_thr
&INPUTHP.docc_thr.description:
Threshold for a comparison of unperturbed occupations
which is needed for the selection of atoms which must
be perturbed. Can be used only when 
find_atpert
 = 1.

&INPUTHP.skip_type.name: skip_type
&INPUTHP.skip_type.description:
skip_type
(i), where i runs over types of atoms.
If 
skip_type
(i)=.true. then no linear-response
calculation will be performed for the i-th atomic type:
in this case 
equiv_type
(i) must be specified, otherwise
the HP code will stop. This option is useful if the
system has atoms of the same type but opposite spin
pollarizations (anti-ferromagnetic case).
This keyword cannot be used when 
find_atpert
 = 1.

&INPUTHP.equiv_type.name: equiv_type
&INPUTHP.equiv_type.description:
equiv_type
(i), where i runs over types of atoms.

equiv_type
(i)=j, will make type i equivalent to type j
(useful when nspin=2). Such a merging of types is done
only at the post-processing stage.
This keyword cannot be used when 
find_atpert
 = 1.

&INPUTHP.perturb_only_atom.name: perturb_only_atom
&INPUTHP.perturb_only_atom.description:
If 
perturb_only_atom
(i)=.true. then only the i-th
atom will be perturbed and considered in the run.
This variable is useful when one wants to split
the whole calculation on parts.


Note:
 this variable has a higher priority than 
skip_type
.

&INPUTHP.start_q.name: start_q
&INPUTHP.start_q.description:
Computes only the q points from 
start_q
 to 
last_q
.


IMPORTANT:
 
start_q
 must be smaller or equal to
the total number of q points found.

&INPUTHP.last_q.name: last_q
&INPUTHP.last_q.description:
Computes only the q points from 
start_q
 to 
last_q
.


IMPORTANT:
 
last_q
 must be smaller or equal to
the total number of q points found.

&INPUTHP.sum_pertq.name: sum_pertq
&INPUTHP.sum_pertq.description:
If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect
pieces of the response occupation matrices for all
q points. This variable should be used only when

start_q
, 
last_q
 and 
perturb_only_atom
 are used.

&INPUTHP.compute_hp.name: compute_hp
&INPUTHP.compute_hp.description:
If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect
pieces of the chi0 and chi matrices (which must have
been produced in previous runs) and then compute
Hubbard parameters. The HP code will look for files
tmp_dir/HP/prefix.chi.i.dat. Note that all files
prefix.chi.i.dat (where i runs over all perturbed
atoms) must be placed in one folder tmp_dir/HP/.

compute_hp
=.true. must be used only when the
calculation was parallelized over perturbations.

&INPUTHP.conv_thr_chi.name: conv_thr_chi
&INPUTHP.conv_thr_chi.description:
Convergence threshold for the response function chi,
which is defined as a trace of the response
occupation matrix.

&INPUTHP.thresh_init.name: thresh_init
&INPUTHP.thresh_init.description:
Initial threshold for the solution of the linear
system (first iteration). Needed to converge the
bare (non-interacting) response function chi0.
The specified value will be multiplied by the
number of electrons in the system.

&INPUTHP.ethr_nscf.name: ethr_nscf
&INPUTHP.ethr_nscf.description:
Threshold for the convergence of eigenvalues during
the iterative diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in
the non-self-consistent-field (NSCF) calculation at
k and k+q points. Note, this quantity is NOT extensive.

&INPUTHP.niter_max.name: niter_max
&INPUTHP.niter_max.description:
Maximum number of iterations in the iterative
solution of the linear-response Kohn-Sham equations.

&INPUTHP.nmix.name: nmix
&INPUTHP.nmix.description:
Number of iterations used in potential mixing
using the modified Broyden method. See:
D.D. Johnson, 
PRB 38, 12807 (1988)
.

&INPUTHP.num_neigh.name: num_neigh
&INPUTHP.num_neigh.description:
Number of nearest neighbors of every Hubbard atom which
will be considered when writting Hubbard V parameters to
the file parameters.out, which can be used in the
subsequent DFT+U+V calculation. This keyword is used only
for DFT+U+V (post-processing stage).

&INPUTHP.lmin.name: lmin
&INPUTHP.lmin.description:
Minimum value of the orbital quantum number of the Hubbard
atoms starting from which (and up to the maximum l in the
system) Hubbard V will be written to the file parameters.out.

lmin
 refers to the orbital quantum number of the atom
corresponding to the first site-index in Hubbard_V(:,:,:).
This keyword is used only for DFT+U+V and only
in the post-processing stage. Example: 
lmin
=1 corresponds to
writing to file V between e.g. oxygen (with p states) and its
neighbors, and including V between transition metals (with d
states) and their neighbors. Instead, when 
lmin
=2 only the
latter will be written to parameters.out.

&INPUTHP.rmax.name: rmax
&INPUTHP.rmax.description:
Maximum distance (in Bohr) between two atoms to search
neighbors (used only at the postprocessing step for
DFT+U+V). This keyword is useful when there
are e.g. defects in the system.

&INPUTHP.dist_thr.name: dist_thr
&INPUTHP.dist_thr.description:
Threshold (in Bohr) for comparing inter-atomic distances
when reconstructing the missing elements of the response
susceptibility in the post-processing step.

&INPUTHP.no_metq0.name: no_metq0
&INPUTHP.no_metq0.description:
If .true. the metallic response term at q=0 is ignored
(i.e. the last term in Eq. (22) in 
PRB 103, 045141 (2021)
).
This is useful for magnetic insulators to avoid the divergence
of the calculation.

&INPUTCOND.prefixt.name: prefixt
&INPUTCOND.prefixt.description:
prefix for the file (as in PWscf) containing all the
regions (left lead + scatt. reg. + right lead)

&INPUTCOND.prefixl.name: prefixl
&INPUTCOND.prefixl.description: prefix for the file containing only the        left lead

&INPUTCOND.prefixs.name: prefixs
&INPUTCOND.prefixs.description: prefix for the file containing the scattering region

&INPUTCOND.prefixr.name: prefixr
&INPUTCOND.prefixr.description: prefix for the file containing only the right lead

&INPUTCOND.tran_prefix.name: tran_prefix
&INPUTCOND.tran_prefix.description:
if tran_prefix is specified the program will save partial results
of a transmission calculation (ikind .GE. 1) in a specific
directory (outdir/tran_prefix.cond_save)

&INPUTCOND.max_seconds.name: max_seconds
&INPUTCOND.max_seconds.default: 1.D+7, or 150 days, i.e. no time limit
&INPUTCOND.max_seconds.description:
jobs stops after max_seconds elapsed time (wallclock time).
It can be enabled only if tran_prefix is specified.

&INPUTCOND.recover.name: recover
&INPUTCOND.recover.description:
restarts a previously interrupted transmission calculation (only if
tran_prefix was specified). It can also be used to gather partial
results from a calculation that was split by using start_e,last_e
and/or start_k,last_k (see corresponding keywords).

&INPUTCOND.band_file.name: band_file
&INPUTCOND.band_file.description: file on which the complex bands are saved

&INPUTCOND.tran_file.name: tran_file
&INPUTCOND.tran_file.description: file where the transmission is written

&INPUTCOND.save_file.name: save_file
&INPUTCOND.save_file.description:
file where the data necessary for PWCOND are written
so that no prefix files of PW are longer needed

&INPUTCOND.fil_loc.name: fil_loc
&INPUTCOND.fil_loc.description:
file on/from which the 2D eigenvalue problem data are
saved/read

&INPUTCOND.lwrite_cond.name: lwrite_cond
&INPUTCOND.lwrite_cond.description: if .t. save the data necessary for PWCOND in save_file

&INPUTCOND.loop_ek.name: loop_ek
&INPUTCOND.loop_ek.description: if .t. the energy loop is outside the k-point loop

&INPUTCOND.lread_cond.name: lread_cond
&INPUTCOND.lread_cond.description: if .t. read the data necessary for PWCOND from save_file

&INPUTCOND.lwrite_loc.name: lwrite_loc
&INPUTCOND.lwrite_loc.description: if .t. save 2D eigenvalue problem result in fil_loc

&INPUTCOND.lread_loc.name: lread_loc
&INPUTCOND.lread_loc.description: if .t. read 2D eigenvalue problem result from fil_loc

&INPUTCOND.ikind.name: ikind
&INPUTCOND.ikind.description:
The kind of conductance calculation:

ikind=0  - just complex band structure (CBS) calculation

ikind=1  - conductance calculation with identical
           left and right leads

ikind=2  - conductance calculation with different
           left and right leads

&INPUTCOND.iofspin.name: iofspin
&INPUTCOND.iofspin.description: spin index for which the calculations are performed

&INPUTCOND.tk_plot.name: tk_plot
&INPUTCOND.tk_plot.description: if > 0, plot T(kx,ky) at each energy in the region [tk_plot x full BZ]

&INPUTCOND.llocal.name: llocal
&INPUTCOND.llocal.description: if .t. calculations are done with only local part of PP

&INPUTCOND.bdl.name: bdl
&INPUTCOND.bdl.description:
right boundary of the left lead (left one is supposed to be at 0)
(in units of lattice parameter "alat" defined in the scf run)

&INPUTCOND.bds.name: bds
&INPUTCOND.bds.description:
right boundary of the scatt. reg. (left one is at 0 if prefixs
is used and = bdl if prefixt is used)
(in units of lattice parameter "alat" defined in the scf run)

&INPUTCOND.bdr.name: bdr
&INPUTCOND.bdr.description:
right boundary of the right lead (left one is at 0 if prefixr
is used and = bds if prefixt is used)
(in units of lattice parameter "alat" defined in the scf run)

&INPUTCOND.nz1.name: nz1
&INPUTCOND.nz1.description: the number of subslabs in the slab (to calculate integrals)

&INPUTCOND.denergy.name: denergy
&INPUTCOND.denergy.description: energy step (if denergy=0.0 the energy is read from the list)

&INPUTCOND.nenergy.name: nenergy
&INPUTCOND.nenergy.description:
number of energies

WARNING: the energy in input file is given in eV taken from Ef,
         and denergy should be negative

&INPUTCOND.start_e.name: start_e
&INPUTCOND.start_e.description:
if start_e > 1, the scattering problem is solved only for those
energies with index between start_e and last_e in the energy list.

NOTE: start_e <= last_e and start_e <= nenergy must be satisfied

&INPUTCOND.last_e.name: last_e
&INPUTCOND.last_e.description:
index of the last energy to be computed. If last_e > nenergy,
then last_e will be automatically set to nenergy.

&INPUTCOND.start_k.name: start_k
&INPUTCOND.start_k.description:
if start_k > 1, the scattering problem is solved only for those
k-points with index between start_k and last_k in the k-point list.
In order to recover the full transmission (i.e. integrated over the
full Brillouin Zone) at the end, perform the partial runs specifying
a value for tran_prefix (the restart directory), then put all the
partial transmission files 'transmission_k#_e#' inside a unique
restart directory and run pwcond.x with recover=.TRUE. (without
specifying any value for start_k and last_k).

NOTE: start_k <= last_k must be satisfied and start_k must also
   not be greater than the actual number of k-point in the list
   (if you compute the grid automatically by specifying the grid
   size and shifts, you can use kpoints.x to check that number).

&INPUTCOND.last_k.name: last_k
&INPUTCOND.last_k.description:
index of the last k-point to be computed. If last_k is bigger than the
actual number of points in the list, then it will be set to that number.

&INPUTCOND.ewind.name: ewind
&INPUTCOND.ewind.description: the energy window for reduction of 2D plane wave basis set (in XY)

&INPUTCOND.orbj_in.name: orbj_in
&INPUTCOND.orbj_in.description: the initial orbital for projecting the transmission

&INPUTCOND.orbj_fin.name: orbj_fin
&INPUTCOND.orbj_fin.description: the final orbital for projecting the transmission

&INPUT.prefix.name: prefix
&INPUT.prefix.description:
Prepended to input/output filenames; must be the same
used in the calculation of unperturbed system.

&INPUT.outdir.name: outdir
&INPUT.outdir.default: value of theESPRESSO_TMPDIRenvironment variable if set;current directory ('./') otherwise

&INPUT.ahc_dir.name: ahc_dir
&INPUT.ahc_dir.description: Directory where the binary files are located.

&INPUT.use_irr_q.name: use_irr_q
&INPUT.use_irr_q.description:
If .true., assume that the q points are on the irreducible grid. In this case,
the data in 
ahc_dir
 must have been actually generated from a calculation
on an irreducible q grid.
Off-diagonal self-energies cannot be computed if use_irr_q = .true.

&INPUT.ahc_nbnd.name: ahc_nbnd
&INPUT.ahc_nbnd.description:
Number of bands for which the electron self-energy is to be computed. Must be
identical to ahc_nbnd of the ph.x run with electron_phonon='ahc'.

&INPUT.ahc_nbndskip.name: ahc_nbndskip
&INPUT.ahc_nbndskip.description:
Number of bands to exclude when computing the self-energy. Must be identical to
ahc_nbndskip of the ph.x run with electron_phonon='ahc'.

&INPUT.flvec.name: flvec
&INPUT.flvec.description: File containing the normalized phonon displacements written by matdyn.x.

&INPUT.eta_eV.name: eta_eV
&INPUT.eta_eV.description:
Magnitude of the small imaginary component included to smooth the energy
denominators, in eV.

&INPUT.temp_kelvin.name: temp_kelvin
&INPUT.temp_kelvin.description: Temperature in Kelvins at which the electron self-energy is calculated.

&INPUT.efermi_eV.name: efermi_eV
&INPUT.efermi_eV.description: Fermi energy of the electrons in eV.

&INPUT.amass_amu.name: amass_amu
&INPUT.amass_amu.description: Mass for each atom type in atomic mass unit.

&INPUT.ahc_win_min_eV.name: ahc_win_min_eV
&INPUT.ahc_win_min_eV.description: Lower bound of active AHC window for the lower Fan term in eV.

&INPUT.ahc_win_max_eV.name: ahc_win_max_eV
&INPUT.ahc_win_max_eV.description: Upper bound of active AHC window for the lower Fan term in eV.

&INPUT.skip_upper.name: skip_upper
&INPUT.skip_upper.description:
If .true., skip calculation of the upper Fan self-energy. Also, truncate the
Debye-Waller self-energy to include only the low-energy band contribution.
(Corresponds to the second term (lower Fan + lower DW) of Eq. (G1-revised) of
J.-M. Lihm and C.-H. Park, PRX 12, 039901(E) (2022).)
If .false., calculate the contribution of both the high-energy and low-energy
bands. In this case, ahc_upfan_iq#.bin files must be present in 
ahc_dir
.

&INPUT.skip_dw.name: skip_dw
&INPUT.skip_dw.description:
If .true., skip calculation of the Debye-Waller self-energy.
If .false., ahc_dw.bin file must be present in 
ahc_dir
.

&INPUT.adiabatic.name: adiabatic
&INPUT.adiabatic.description:
If .true., use the adiabatic approximation when computing the Fan self-energy
by ignoring the phonon frequency in the denominator. This approximation is known
to be inaccurate and even divergent in some materials (S. PoncÃ© et al., J. Chem.
Phys. 143, 102813 (2015)). Therefore, this keyword should be used only for
experimental or debugging purposes.

&INPUT.fildyn.name: fildyn
&INPUT.fildyn.description: input file containing the dynamical matrix

&INPUT.asr.name: asr
&INPUT.asr.description:
Indicates the type of Acoustic Sum Rule imposed.

Allowed values:
            




'no'
 :



no Acoustic Sum Rules imposed 
(default)

            






'simple'
 :



previous implementation of the asr used
(3 translational asr imposed by correction of
 the diagonal elements of the dynamical matrix)
            






'crystal'
 :



3 translational asr imposed by optimized
correction of the dyn. matrix (projection)
            






'one-dim'
 :



3 translational asr + 1 rotational asr imposed
by optimized correction of the dyn. mat. (the
rotation axis is the direction of periodicity; it
will work only if this axis considered is one of
the Cartesian axis).
            






'zero-dim'
 :



3 translational asr + 3 rotational asr imposed
by optimized correction of the dyn. mat.
            





Note that in certain cases, not all the rotational asr
can be applied (e.g. if there are only 2 atoms in a
molecule or if all the atoms are aligned, etc.).  In
these cases the supplementary asr are canceled during
the orthonormalization procedure (see below).

Finally, in all cases except 
'no'
 a simple correction
on the effective charges is performed (same as in the
previous implementation).

&INPUT.remove_interaction_blocks.name: remove_interaction_blocks
&INPUT.remove_interaction_blocks.description:
If .true. lines and rows corresponding to atoms that are not displaced
are set to 0. This can be used for ph.x calculations with nat_todo set
in ph.x, to remove the interaction between the diplaced and fixed parts of the system.

&INPUT.axis.name: axis
&INPUT.axis.description: indicates the rotation axis for a 1D system (1=Ox, 2=Oy, 3=Oz)

&INPUT.lperm.name: lperm
&INPUT.lperm.description:
if .true. then calculate Gamma-point mode contributions to
dielectric permittivity tensor

&INPUT.lplasma.name: lplasma
&INPUT.lplasma.description:
if .true. then calculate Gamma-point mode effective plasma
frequencies, automatically triggers 
lperm
 = .true.

&INPUT.filout.name: filout
&INPUT.filout.description:
output file containing phonon frequencies and normalized
phonon displacements (i.e. eigenvectors divided by the
square root of the mass and then normalized; they are
not orthogonal)

&INPUT.fileig.name: fileig
&INPUT.fileig.description:
output file containing phonon frequencies and eigenvectors
of the dynamical matrix (they are orthogonal)

&INPUT.filmol.name: filmol
&INPUT.filmol.description: as above, in a format suitable for molden

&INPUT.filxsf.name: filxsf
&INPUT.filxsf.description: as above, in axsf format suitable for xcrysden

&INPUT.loto_2d.name: loto_2d
&INPUT.loto_2d.description: set to .true. to activate two-dimensional treatment of LO-TO splitting.

&INPUT.el_ph_nsig.name: el_ph_nsig
&INPUT.el_ph_nsig.description:
The number of double-delta smearing values used in an electron-phonon
coupling calculation.

&INPUT.el_ph_sigma.name: el_ph_sigma
&INPUT.el_ph_sigma.description:
The spacing of double-delta smearing values used in an electron-phonon
coupling calculation.

&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.initial_prefix.description: prefix of the initial pw.x calculation.

&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.final_prefix.name: final_prefix
&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.final_prefix.description: prefix of the final pw.x calculation.

&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.initial_dir.name: initial_dir
&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.initial_dir.description:

&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.final_dir.name: final_dir
&OSCDFT_ET_NAMELIST.final_dir.description:

i.e. the same as in pw.x.

&OSCDFT_PP_NAMELIST.outdir.name: outdir
&OSCDFT_PP_NAMELIST.outdir.description: directory containing the input data, i.e. the same as in pw.x

&INTERPOLATION.method.name: method
&INTERPOLATION.method.description: The interpolation method to be used

&INTERPOLATION.miller_max.name: miller_max
&INTERPOLATION.miller_max.description:
The maximum Miller index used to automatically generate the set of symmetry inequivalent Star vectors
                  (only for 
method
 == 'fourier-diff' or 'fourier')

&INTERPOLATION.check_periodicity.name: check_periodicity
&INTERPOLATION.check_periodicity.description:
If .TRUE. a (time consuming) step is performed, to check whether all the Star functions have
                  the correct lattice periodicity (only for 
method
 == 'fourier-diff' or 'fourier') .

                  For automatically generated Star functions this should never occur by construction, and the program
                  will stop and exit in case one Star function with wrong periodicity is found (useful for
                  debugging and program sanity check).

                  If additional user-defined Star vectors are specified (see optional card 
USER_STARS
),
                  the program will print a WARNING in case one Star function with wrong periodicity is found.

&INTERPOLATION.p_metric.name: p_metric
&INTERPOLATION.p_metric.description:
The exponent of the distance in the IDW method ( only for 
method
 == 'idw' or 'idw-sphere')

&INTERPOLATION.scale_sphere.name: scale_sphere
&INTERPOLATION.scale_sphere.description:
The search radius for 
method
 == 'idw-sphere', is Rmin * scale_sphere, where Rmin is the
                  minimum distance found between the uniform grid of k-points.

                  If scale_sphere is too small, some k-points of the path might not see enough uniform grid points
                  to average energies, whereas for large values the method becomes equal to 
method
 == 'idw'.

ROUGHNESS.RoughN.name: RoughN
ROUGHNESS.RoughN.description: Number of terms included in the roughness functional

ROUGHNESS.RoughC.name: RoughC
ROUGHNESS.RoughC.description:
Coefficients for the terms included in the roughness functional.
                                They can be explicitely given or 'automatic' can be specified instead of numbers
                                to use default coefficients.

USER_STARS.NUser.name: NUser

 when providing

&INPUTPP.fileout.description: basename of the cppp.x output files

directory containing the CP trajectory files (.evp .pos .cel ...)

&PPACF.code_num.name: code_num
&PPACF.code_num.description:
Select from which code to read output files.
  1 = Quantum ESPRESSO
  2 = VASP
      The codes will read vasprun.xml and CHGCAR from VASP
      calculations.
      Please note that in VASP-based analysis:
      - Core charge is ignored.
      - The ppacf-from-VASP-read-in only works for VASP
        calculations done in PBE, revPBE, vdW-DF, vdW-DF2, or vdW-DF-cx
      - The ppacf-from-VASP-read-in only always uses the full Ecnl kernel
        for coupling-constant scaling analysis of vdW-DF versions.
      - Wavefunction based analysis (Fock exchange energy and
        Kohn-Sham kinetic energy) are not available from VASP
      - When 
lplot
 = .True., the code will also print out
        charge density in prefix.chg (prefix.chg1 and prefix.chg2
        save the spin-up and spin-down components in case of
        spin-polarized calculations), which can be processed by 
pp.x.

&PPACF.vdW_analysis.name: vdW_analysis
&PPACF.vdW_analysis.description:
Select type of vdw kernel table used in ppacf coupling-constant scaling
analysis of nonlocal-correlations in vdW-DF versions:
- vdW_analysis = 0: Full Ecnl kenel of vdW-DF method
- vdW_analysis = 1: The cumulant- or susceptibility-Ecnl kernel component
- vdW_analysis = 2: The pure-vdW-Ecnl kernel component
See IOP JCPM (2020) for presentation of the latter two (non-default) options

&PLOT.output_format.name: output_format
&PLOT.output_format.description:
(ignored on 1D plot)

0  = format suitable for gnuplot   (1D)

1  = obsolete format no longer supported

2  = format suitable for plotrho   (2D)

3  = format suitable for XCRYSDEN  (2D or user-supplied 3D region)

4  = obsolete format no longer supported

5  = format suitable for XCRYSDEN  (3D, using entire FFT grid)

6  = format as gaussian cube file  (3D)
     (can be read by many programs)

7  = format suitable for gnuplot   (2D) x, y, f(x,y)

 is in alat units !

&PLOT.nx.description:

phi(i)   = 2 pi * (i - 1)/(nx-1), i=1, nx

&PLOT.e1.description:
3D vectors which determine the plotting parallelepiped
(if present, must be orthogonal)


e1
, 
e2
, and 
e3
 are in alat units !

&PLOT.ny.name: ny
&PLOT.ny.description:
Number of points in the polar plane:

phi(i)   = 2 pi * (i - 1)/(nx-1), i=1, nx
theta(j) =   pi * (j - 1)/(ny-1), j=1, ny

&PLOT.nz.name: nz
&PLOT.nz.description:
Number of points in the parallelepiped:

rho(i,j,k) = rho( x0 + e1 * (i-1)/nx
                 + e2 * (j-1)/ny
                 + e3 * (k-1)/nz ),
            i = 1, nx ; j = 1, ny ; k = 1, nz

- If 
output_format

  are used to determine the grid to plot.

- If 
output_format
 = 5 (XCRYSDEN), the above variables
  are ignored, the entire FFT grid is written in the
  XCRYSDEN format - works for any crystal axis (VERY FAST)

- If 
e1
, 
e2
, 
e3
, 
x0
 are present,
  and 
e1
, 
e2
, 
e3
 are parallel to xyz

  grid that approximately covers the parallelepiped
  defined by 
e1
